title: Finite filtration of a finitely generated subsheaf of the constant sheaf
statement: Let X be a topological space in which the intersection of any two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact. Let K be a subsheaf of the constant abelian sheaf \underline{\mathbf Z}_X [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] generated by finitely many sections over quasi-compact opens. Then K has a finite filtration 0=K_0 \subset K_1 \subset \cdots \subset K_n=K such that each successive quotient K_i/K_{i-1} fits into a short exact sequence 0 \to j'_! \underline{\mathbf Z}_V \to j_! \underline{\mathbf Z}_U \to K_i/K_{i-1} \to 0 for quasi-compact opens V and U of X and their open immersions j',j, where j'_! and j_! are extension by zero [lem-sc-topological-extension-by-zero-stalks].

proof.text: Apply the uniform integer stalk-bound lemma to the given finitely generated subsheaf. Fix its isomorphisms e_x and its bound b. Prove the finite filtration by induction on b, generalizing the subsheaf K and its monomorphism into C.

source.place: Lemma 0A38, finite normalization and bounded integer-value filtration

proof.text: For b=0 every stalk image is zero. Its map into C_x followed by e_x is injective, using TopCat.Presheaf.stalk_mono_of_mono and AddCommGrpCat.mono_iff_injective. Hence each K_x is zero; TopCat.Sheaf.isZero_iff_stalkFunctor_obj_isZero implies K is zero. Take m=0 and the sole stage K with identity terminal isomorphism. All indexed quotient requirements are vacuous.

source.place: Lemma 0A38, zero initial stage; Mathlib Topology/Sheaves/Abelian.lean and Stalks.lean

proof.text: For bound b+1, use the one-layer lemma to get l:L to K, with L finitely generated and bounded by b, and a short exact presentation of coker l. The induction hypothesis gives the filtration of L. Append K to its object tuple using Fin.snoc; the new arrow is the terminal isomorphism to L followed by l, transported along the tuple equalities. Old arrows are transported along the same equalities. All are monic by composition.

Append coker l and its presenting complex to the quotient and short-complex tuples. Transport old cokernel isomorphisms with CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.mapIso; for the new arrow use the same lemma and the terminal isomorphism to L. Fin.lastCases verifies every short-exact and compact-open condition, while Fin.snoc preserves the zero initial stage and makes the terminal stage exactly K. Repeated stages are allowed by the unchanged statement, so no deletion is necessary.
